Perfect classification

This pipeline demonstrates methylation-based tissue-of-origin classification using a literature-curated 25-gene panel. COAD and LAML are perfectly classified (5/5), while PRAD and BRCA show cross-classification due to overlapping methylation patterns. Key findings: HOXA5 is the strongest tissue discriminator (Δ=0.405), LAML separates clearly in PCA, and CD274 is the most important random forest feature.

Tissue-Specific Methylation Heatmap

Mean beta values per gene per cancer type, sorted by inter-cancer variance. Genes at top show most tissue-specific patterns.

PCA — Cancer Type Separation

PC1 (25%) separates blood (LAML) from solid tumors. PC2 (16.3%) separates prostate (PRAD). Together 3 PCs explain 53.4% of variance.

Random Forest Classifier

Leave-one-out cross-validation, n=500 trees. COAD and LAML perfectly classified. CD274, CDH1, HOXA5 are top discriminating features.

Gene-Gene Methylation Correlation

Pearson correlation across 30 samples. PAX6-GATA4 (r=0.74) and RUNX1-TET2 (r=0.62) show strongest co-methylation.
